To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in vitro priming with LNCaP tumor cells or with LNCaPs membrane preparations is more effective than priming with prostate specific antigen (2) priming of female cells is more effective than of male cells and (3) addition of exogenous interleukin 2 is required for optimal priming of female spleen cells.
intact LNCaP tumor cells are superior to membrane preparations of the same cells and to PSA as immunogens for in vitro induction of anti-tumor antibodies.

(i) the efficiency of in vitro priming of spleen cells by prostate antigens was dependent on the type of antigen and on the donor sex; (ii) the efficiency of the in vitro immunization of spleen cells was enhanced by addition of IL2; (iii) the immunized cells could be used as a source for generation of monoclonal antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective immunization procedure for in vitro primed splenocytes.
the development of an effective in vitro immunization system for human cells.
the production of antibodies to the prostate antigen by in vitro immunization of human splenocytes with intact prostate cells, a membrane preparation of prostate cells or prostate specific antigen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective in vitro immunization is obtained with LNCaP cell membranes and spleen cells of female origin.
the most efficient immunization is achieved by male spleen cells primed in vitro with intact LNCaP tumor cells.
in vitro priming of human splenocytes with prostate antigen is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficiency of immunization of spleen cells by three kinds of human prostate antigen was dependent on the type of antigen, donor sex, and addition of IL-1.
in vitro immunization of human splenocytes is a useful tool to study antigen specific immune responses and to produce monoclonal antibodies to prostate antigents.
the most efficient in vitro immunization of human splenocytes with prostate antigens was obtained with LNCaP cell membrane preparation and mixed lymphocyte culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in vitro priming of spleen cells by prostate antigens is feasible and that the efficiency of the immunization can be significantly enhanced by addition of IL2 to the culture medium of female splenocytes.
the efficiency of immunization by prostate antigens in vitro can be improved by the choice of antigen and by the addition of IL- 2.
in vitro priming of splenocytes with LNCaP and PMA is a useful approach for generating monoclonal antibodies to prostate antigents.
